comments.content:
This block is only reachable from the direct-install path (`installAsset(isUpdate, filePath, …)`), which is itself only used when the orchestrator parks the file (`InstallPolicy.InstallWhileForeground`). For the two most common configurations the skip tag therefore never gets persisted:

1. Default system installer: `SilentInstallerDispatcher` → `AndroidInstaller.install()` always returns `InstallOutcome.DELEGATED_TO_SYSTEM` (`core/data/src/androidMain/.../AndroidInstaller.kt:113`), so `installOutcome == InstallOutcome.COMPLETED` is never true and the `skippedReleaseTag` is never written — the app immediately re-advertises the release the user just declined to install.
2. Shizuku/Dhizuku: `installAsset` sets `InstallPolicy.AlwaysInstall` for those installer types, so `DefaultDownloadOrchestrator.runInstall()` performs the install itself and the outcome surfaces in `observeOrchestratorEntry`'s `OrchestratorStage.Completed` branch — which has no skip handling at all.

There is also a third leak: when a signing-fingerprint mismatch defers the install to `overrideSigningKeyWarning()`, `skipDetectedLatest` is not carried over (only `pendingIsUpdate` is), so the skip is silently dropped after a successful override. And if `validateApk` returned `ExtractionFailed`, `validatedApkInfo` stays null and the block is skipped even though the install completed.

Consider recording the skip from a single place that sees every completion path (e.g. the `Completed` branch, plus the override path) and falling back to `_state.value.installedApp?.packageName` when `validatedApkInfo` is null, rather than gating it on `== COMPLETED` inside this one code path.

Therefore, the strongest comment: the skip is applied only in DetailsViewModel.installAsset(filePath) — reachable only when the policy is InstallWhileForeground with a silent backend (e.g., ROOT) — while:
- the default installer returns DELEGATED_TO_SYSTEM (fails `== COMPLETED`), and
- Shizuku/Dhizuku use AlwaysInstall so the orchestrator performs the install (installOutcome COMPLETED in the observe loop's Completed branch, which has no skip handling).

So for most users the skip tag is never persisted, defeating the feature. Suggest centralizing the skip-recording in the observe loop's Completed branch (and/or a shared helper), and reconsidering the COMPLETED-only guard for delegated installs.
